Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qov.ph S. 2024 OILG OPINION NO E_ JUL 08 2025 HON. MACARIO V. TINGSON Mayor, Municipality of Tukuran Province of Zamboanga del Sur Dear Mayor Tingson: This pertains to your letter-request dated October I, 2024, seeking this Department's permission or authority to hire the services of Atty. Lucio Orio Tan, Jr. until such time that the position of Municipal Legal Officer as Head of the Municipal Legal Office of Tukuran is filled. In your letter, you belabored the necessity of engaging the services of Atty. Tan due to the volume and complexity of legal matters requiring expertise that cannot be addressed internally. It is intimated that in August 2023, the Municipality of Tukuran engaged the services of Atty. Tan as Legal Consultant. However, the Commission on Audit (COA), through an Audit Observation Memorandum (AOM) recommended that the Municipality of Tukuran seek prior approval from the Office of the Solicitor General (OSG). However, it is your submission that COA Circular No. 2021-003 does not apply to LGUs, as stated in Item 5.0 (Non-Applicability to Local Govemment Units on [COA] Circular No. 2021- 003, dated July 16, 2021) thereof, which reads that the "aforesaid circular does not apply to LGU, as there are specific provisions for provincial, city and municipal legal offices under RA No. 7160, or the Local Govemment Code of 1991". Hence, your subject request In response thereto, this Department respectfully opines that its approval is not required for Local Government Units (LGUs) to hire or engage the services of private lawyers as legal consultants, as the authority for such contracts falls within the purview of the sanggunian concerned or as provided by ordinance or law. On this score, attention is respectfully directed to pertinent provisions of the Local Government Code (Republic Act 7160, hereinafter referred to as the Code), thus: Section 22(c) of the Code provides: "Unless otherwise provided in this Code, no contract may be entered into by the local chief executive in behalf of the local government unit without prior authorization by the sanggunian concerned. A legible copy of such contract shall be posted at a conspicuous place in the provincial capitol or the city, municipality or barangay hall." (Emphasis ours) "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline NO. (02) 8876 3454

, Section 444(b)(I )(vi) of the Code states: "Upon authorization by the sangguniang bayan, represent the municipality in all its business transactions and sign on its behalf all bonds, contracts, and obligations, and such other documents made pursuant to law or ordinance. Xxx" Gleaned from the afore-cited provisions, the municipal mayor, upon prior authorization from the sangguniang bayan, may enter into contracts on behalf of the municipality, including hiring consultants. Accordingly, what the law requires is prior authorization from the sanggunian unless already covered by ordinance or law. Stated differently, the authority required by law for the Mayor to enter contracts falls within the ambit of the sanggunian—and not from this Department. It should be emphasized, however, that prior authorization from the sangggunian as contemplated in the Code is not absolute. The Mayor may represent the municipality in all its contracts san prior authorization from the sanggunian as long as there is either a law or ordinance that authorizes him/her to do so. This has been clarified by the Supreme Court Quisumbingl and reiterated in Verceles Jr. v. Commission on Audie, thus: "The prior authorization for the local chief executive to enter into contracts on behalf of the local government units may be in the form of an appropriating ordinance passed for the year which specifically covers the project, cost, or contract to be entered into by the local government unit. If the project or program is identified in the appropriation ordinance in sufficient detail, then there is no more need to obtain a separate or additional authority from the sanggunian. In such case, the project and the cost are already identified and approved by the sanggunian through the appropriation ordinance. To require the local chief executive to secure another authorization for a project that has been specifically identified and approved by the sanggunian is antithetical to a responsive local government envisioned in the Constitution and in the LGC. On the other hand, the need for a covering contract arises when the project is identified in generic terms. The covering contract must also be approved by the sanggunian." Having laid down the foregoing, we note that your intent to engage the services of Atty. Tan appears to be through Negotiated Procurement, which is governed by Republic Act No. 9184 (Government Procurement Reform Act), as amended, and its Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR). In this regard, it bears noting that engagement Of services of individual personnel under Contract of Service or Job Order is distinct from the procurement of Consulting Services. The following are some of the noted distinctions: Contract of Service or Job Order are covered by COA Rules3, while a Consulting Service is governed by Republic Act (RA) 91844, as amended. G.R NO. 175527, December 8, 2008. G.R. NO. 211553. September 13. 2016. ' GPPB Resolution NO. 09-2012, dated 27 April 2012. The Govemment Procurement Reform Act. Page 2 of 4

The Government Procurement Policy Board (GPPB) in PM02-2012m dated November 21, 2012, opined that "[Ilf the desired service would require adequate external technical and professional capability and expertise that are beyond the existing capacity of the procuring entity, then the rules and regulation on the procurement of consulting services under RA 9184 and its IRR shall be applicable. Conversely, RA 9184 and its IRR will not apply in the hiring of individual personnel under Job Order or Contract of Service because the engagement does not require that level of expertise as primary consideration for its selection, but merely pertains to the engagement of ordinary piece of work or intermittent job of short duration. " Secondly, Job Order or Contract of Service5, which does not cover special or technical skills or where the functions to be performed are clerical or administrative in nature of where the work is also performed by the regular personnel of the agency, may be entered into only when done in the exigency of the service and it is not feasible for the agency to hire said services under a casual or contractual appointment. On the other hand, the services of consultants may be engaged by any procuring entity for government projects or related activities of such magnitude and/or scope as would require a level of expertise or attention beyond the optimum in-house capability of the procuring entity concerned and consistent with the Government's policy not to compete with the private sector.6 Pertinently, the GPPB-TSO Opinion in NPM No. 154-2015 is instructive. It opines that the procurement of the services of individual consultants is covered by RA 9184, as amended, and its IRR. Section 53.7 of the IRR of RA 9184 allows the procurement of Individual Consultants through Negotiated Procurement under the Highly Technical Consultants modality, provided that the work to be done is (i) highly technical or propriety; or (ii) primarily confidential or policy-determining, where trust and confidence are the primary considerations for the hiring of the individual consultant. In line with this, the term of the individual consultants shall, at the most, be on a six-month basis, renewable at the option of the HOPE [Head of Procuring Entity], but in no case shall exceed the term of the latter. On the approval of the OSG, we refer to the Revised Guidelines on Deputation of private Lawyers and Special Attorneys dated December 15, 2015 which explicitly stated under Item thereof that "(t)he OSG, not being the lawyer of Local Govemment Units, cannot deputize private lawyers to handle LGU cases. Hence, all requests for deputation of private lawyers shall be denied outright " On the approval of the COA, we defer to COA's findings through the issued Audit Observation Memorandum in due deference to its constitutional mandate. It has the highest degree of competence concerning its guidelines, Thus, we submit that any irregularities in the contracts or payments not compliant to laws, established policies as well as the Commission's rules and procedures may lead to disallowance during audit. s CSC Memorandum Circular No. 24, s. 2002, entitled: Clarifications on Policy Guidelines for Contract of Services. 6 Annex "B" — General Principles on Consulting Services. Notwithstanding. please note that this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities or the courts We hope to have guided you accordingly Very truly yours, By Authonty of the Secretary ATTY.
